article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: Shiva × New York City Diesel
Breeder: Bonguru Beans
THC Content: 22%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Red grapefruit, dried fruit, sweet citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Medium
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate to advanced

Shiesel comes from an era when combining two famous cannabis lines could still produce something genuinely unexpected rather than another minor variation on an established commercial formula. Bonguru Beans paired a specially selected Shiva used by Dutch medical growers with New York City Diesel from Soma Seeds , aiming to bring Shiva’s dense, hash-heavy physical potency into contact with the exotic fruit and citrus character that made NYC Diesel famous. The experiment worked well enough for Shiesel to earn a place in Ed Rosenthal ’s The Big Book of Buds Vol. 2, where the cultivar was described as an indica-dominant hybrid combining a profound body stone with a sweet-and-sour dried-fruit palate.

What makes the strain memorable is the contrast between those qualities. The flower can begin with grapefruit and fermented fruit sweetness, then move toward darker hash, spice, earth, and Diesel pungency. Effects follow the same pattern in reverse: the exotic flavor may suggest something bright and energetic, yet Shiva quickly makes its presence known through a deep physical stone. Shiesel is therefore not simply another Diesel cross. It is a distinctly old-school piece of European marijuana breeding, bringing a compact Dutch indica-style plant together with one of Soma’s most recognizable aromatic cultivars.
Genetics and Lineage

Bonguru Beans bred Shiesel from a special Shiva selection crossed with Soma’s New York City Diesel. Historical genetic indexes identify the Shiva more specifically with old Positronics material, while contemporary breeder copy described the mother as a special plant selected from Dutch medical-grower stock. Positronics’ Shiva was itself known as compact, powerful cannabis with a roughly seven-to-eight-week flowering period—traits that help explain the shorter, heavier side of the resulting hybrid.

The New York City Diesel parent supplies a much more colorful aromatic background. Soma Seeds currently identifies NYC Diesel as Mexican Sativa × Afghani and describes ripe red grapefruit as the strain’s defining smell and flavor. The breeder also characterizes it as sativa leaning, with a considerably longer 12–13-week flowering cycle. Crossing that plant with Shiva effectively pulled two opposing sets of traits together: exotic grapefruit and cerebral Diesel qualities on one side, compact structure and a powerful hash-style body stone on the other.

Because Shiesel was released as an F1, growers should expect meaningful phenotype variation rather than clone-like uniformity. Bonguru’s historical description specifically noted that individual plants could reveal noticeable differences between the parents. Some expressions lean harder toward Shiva in plant form and physical effects; others reveal more of NYC Diesel’s citrus, fruit, and stretch. That variability is part of the cultivar’s identity rather than evidence that the genetics are unstable or incorrectly labeled.
Effects and Experience

The first noticeable feature of the high is its weight. Contemporary descriptions emphasize that Shiva contributes most strongly to the psychoactive character, producing an effect centered in the body that can feel profound, hashy, and increasingly narcotic. Ed Rosenthal’s published profile even warned that inexperienced consumers could find the stone unexpectedly overwhelming. The onset may initially bring a pleasant mental shift, heightened appetite, and greater interest in music or sensory experiences, but physical heaviness tends to become the dominant theme.

As the session deepens, movement can become less appealing and ordinary tasks substantially more difficult. The mind does not necessarily become blank; rather, thought can become detached and trippy while the body settles into a slower rhythm. That makes the strain more appropriate for evenings, relaxed social settings, movies, music, or situations where concentration and coordination are no longer important. Lower servings may preserve more of the uplifting Diesel influence, while larger amounts favor the Shiva side and can move rapidly toward couch-lock.

No trustworthy breeder THC percentage survives for the original release, so potency should not be reduced to an invented number. Historical assessments consistently characterized the flower as strong, and its reputation was based on experienced effect rather than laboratory marketing. Modern consumers encountering authenticated material should rely on the actual batch analysis and begin conservatively, since high-THC weed can produce dizziness, anxiety, memory impairment, or excessive sedation when consumed beyond personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

There are no clinical trials evaluating Shiesel as a treatment for a specific medical condition. Its heavy body effects may explain why some medical marijuana consumers historically gravitated toward it for discomfort, appetite problems, difficulty relaxing, or nighttime use, but those experiences cannot establish strain-specific medical efficacy.

Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly suggests modest benefits for some forms of chronic pain, while cannabinoid medications have established uses for certain forms of chemotherapy-related nausea, appetite loss associated with HIV/AIDS, and specific seizure disorders. Research on sleep and many other commonly claimed uses remains less certain. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health stresses that effects vary according to cannabinoid composition, formulation, and dose.

That distinction is particularly relevant for an older seed strain without standardized cannabinoid testing. A heavily sedating phenotype could feel useful to one patient and uncomfortably impairing to another. THC may also cause dizziness, anxiety, sleepiness, altered judgment, or medication interactions. Medical users should therefore base decisions on current product testing and professional guidance rather than assuming the historical “narcotic” reputation translates directly into a medical benefit.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

New York City Diesel dominates much of the aromatic conversation. Soma describes its parent strain through ripe red grapefruit, and Shiesel preserves that exotic citrus quality while adding darker fruit and hash from Shiva. The Big Book of Buds characterized the flavor as sweet-and-sour dried fruit, which remains one of the most useful descriptions of the cultivar because it captures both the sugary and fermented sides of the profile.

Fresh flower may open with grapefruit peel, sweet citrus, and dried fruit before revealing sourness, earth, spice, and resin underneath. Grower accounts have occasionally described grapefruit aromas powerful enough for one plant to dominate the smell of an entire mixed garden, illustrating just how strongly the NYC Diesel side can emerge in selected phenotypes. Shiva prevents the profile from becoming purely fruity, adding a darker hash-like character that becomes particularly apparent on the finish.

No authentic laboratory terpene panel from Bonguru Beans has been located. Assigning fixed percentages of limonene, myrcene, caryophyllene, or another terpene would therefore create false precision. What is documented is far more useful: grapefruit and exotic fruit from NYC Diesel meeting dense, resinous, hash-oriented Shiva character. Proper curing is especially important because the brightest citrus components will fade sooner than earth and hash when marijuana is exposed to excessive heat or oxygen.
Growing Information

Shiesel begins deceptively compact. Contemporary documentation describes a plant that can look quite short early in development, only to experience a noticeable growth spurt partway through flowering. Plants can ultimately approach roughly a meter in height, while the finished colas display the large size and heavy crystal coverage associated with the Shiva parent. Both soil and hydroponic cultivation were recommended historically.

Flowering generally falls between eight and ten weeks. The Big Book of Buds gives approximately 63–70+ days with phenotype-dependent variation, while original breeder material also centered the strain around roughly nine weeks. Because the cross is an F1, forcing every plant onto the same harvest date makes less sense than following trichome development, calyx swelling, aroma, and overall maturity. The breeder characterized yield as moderate rather than extraordinary, suggesting that Shiesel was selected primarily around smoking quality rather than maximum commercial production.

Cultivators should also expect the parent plants to pull architecture in different directions. A Shiva-leaning phenotype can remain shorter and denser, while a Diesel-heavy expression may stretch more noticeably. Early canopy observation is therefore more useful than assuming every plant requires the same training. Moderate topping or branch positioning can help manage more vigorous examples, but heavy intervention late in flowering may unnecessarily stress plants already committing energy to large resinous colas.

Resin is one of the cultivar’s strongest horticultural traits. Historical breeder commentary specifically praised Shiesel as useful hash material, and the Shiva side is associated with substantial gland production. Mature flowers benefit from good airflow and careful humidity management, especially when dense colas begin accumulating weight. A controlled dry followed by patient curing will preserve far more of the grapefruit and dried-fruit character than a rapid high-temperature finish.
FAQ
What strain is Shiesel?

Shiesel is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by Bonguru Beans from a specially selected Shiva crossed with Soma Seeds’ New York City Diesel. Contemporary documentation places it around 75% indica and 25% sativa.
Who bred Shiesel?

Bonguru Beans created the original strain. The breeder was active during the early-2000s Dutch cannabis scene and also released cultivars such as RockStar. Shiesel appeared in Ed Rosenthal’s The Big Book of Buds Vol. 2.
What does Shiesel taste like?

Expect sweet-and-sour dried fruit, ripe grapefruit, citrus, earth, hash, spice, and Diesel funk. NYC Diesel contributes most of the exotic fruit character, while Shiva adds a heavier resinous and hash-like finish.
Is Shiesel indica or sativa?

The original cultivar is primarily indica, with contemporary references placing it near 75% indica and 25% sativa. Its effects support that classification: NYC Diesel adds some mental lift and exotic flavor, but Shiva provides the deeper physical stone.
How long does Shiesel take to flower?

Historical sources place flowering around 8–10 weeks, with The Big Book of Buds listing approximately 63–70+ days depending on phenotype. The F1 population can vary enough that maturity should be judged plant by plant.
Final Thoughts on Shiesel

Shiesel represents an especially interesting moment in Dutch cannabis breeding because neither parent disappears inside the cross. Soma’s New York City Diesel contributes its unmistakable grapefruit, exotic fruit, and sativa-leaning personality, while the selected Shiva supplies dense resin, hash flavor, compact early growth, and a far heavier body effect. The result is not a generic Diesel hybrid but a cultivar with a distinct two-part identity.

Its documentation is unusually strong for a strain that has become difficult to find. Bonguru Beans’ genetics were recorded in contemporary breeding indexes, while Ed Rosenthal included the cultivar in The Big Book of Buds Vol. 2 with its Shiva × New York Diesel lineage, indica-dominant classification, flowering range, flavor, effect, and growth characteristics intact.

For growers, the attraction lies in an F1 population offering genuine phenotype hunting: shorter Shiva-influenced plants, more expressive Diesel-leaning individuals, substantial resin, large colas, and flowering around eight to ten weeks. For consumers, the defining progression runs from grapefruit and sweet-sour fruit into earth, hash, and a profound body stone.

That combination gives Shiesel lasting value as an old-school strain reference . It connects Positronics-era Shiva genetics with one of Soma Seeds’ defining cultivars, producing weed that manages to be exotic in flavor and traditional in effect at the same time—grapefruit Diesel on the palate, powerful hashy indica underneath.
